## Result

**What I built** — `landing/index.html`, a single self-contained file (no build step). It opens the painting's story in Mondrian's own visual language:

- **Hero**: title, year, movement, medium, collection as chips, plus a CSS rendering of the painting — large red square top-right, small blue square bottom-left, small yellow rectangle bottom-right, thick black lines on a white ground.
- **3D relief**: a Three.js canvas (the only allowed CDN) renders the composition as a raised relief you can drag to rotate.
- **Three story sections**: the painter (Piet Mondrian, 1872–1944, Dutch), the movement (De Stijl, founded NL 1917 by van Doesburg and Mondrian; Neoplasticism's rules), and why it matters (asymmetric balance → reference for modern graphic design and architecture).
- **CTA**: "Read more at the source" linking to the Wikipedia URL the fact sheet gives.

**How I know it's right**
- Every claim traces to `FACTSHEET.md`; I added nothing beyond it (no dates, places, or interpretations not in the sheet).
- I opened the file in a browser: hero, 3D canvas, and CTA all render (verified by screenshots). One bug found and fixed — the outer grid put the thin black rails in the wide columns (page rendered mostly black); I swapped `grid-template-columns` to `var(--line) 1fr var(--line)` and re-verified.
- Only two external requests: Google Fonts and `cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js`, matching the allowed network.

**Assumptions I made** (the brief left these open)
- The painting image can't be fetched (only Google Fonts + three.js are reachable), so I drew the composition with CSS and Three.js from the fact sheet's description rather than embedding an image.
- "Speaks Mondrian's visual language" = white ground, primary red/blue/yellow, black grid lines, hard rectangles, asymmetric balance — applied to layout, type, and the 3D relief.
- Used a neutral grotesque (Archivo) as the typeface since no specific font was specified.

**Open limits**
- The 3D relief is an interpretation of the described composition, not a pixel-accurate reproduction (no source image available offline).
- I could not test the page on a network that actually blocks everything else; I verified layout and asset references, not network isolation behavior.
